title: Self-Blinding and Counterfactual Self-Simulation Mitigate Biases and Sycophancy in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The paper did not measure any aspect of faith or religion. The benchmarks measured demographic bias based on race (Asian, Black, Hispanic, white) and gender (male/female), as well as sycophantic bias where the model agrees with the user's stated position in a dispute.
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion, as it was not a variable included in the study. The key findings relate to the ineffectiveness of simple prompting to mitigate race, gender, and sycophantic biases, and the effectiveness of a 'self-blinding' method where models can query a version of themselves that lacks the biasing information.
